[[Club Nacional de Football|Nacional]] won their 43rd Primera División title after defeating [[Defensor Sporting]] in the season-ending final. ==Teams== Sixteen teams will compete in the Primera División this season. Thirteen teams remained from the 2009–10 season. [[Atenas de San Carlos|Atenas]], [[Club Sportivo Cerrito|Cerrito]], and [[Cerro Largo FC|Cerro Largo]] were relegated after accumulating the fewest points in the season aggregate table. They were replaced by [[El Tanque Sisley]], [[C.A. Bella Vista|Bella Vista]], and [[Miramar Misiones]], the 2009–10 Segunda División winner, runner-up, and playoff winner, respectively. All of the new teams are making repeat appearances. All the teams in this season are from [[Montevideo]], except [[Tacuarembó F.C.]], who comes from [[Tacuarembó|the city they are named for]]. {{location map+ |Uruguay |float=right |width=200 |caption=Locations of the 2010–11 Primera División teams |places= {{location map~ |Uruguay |lat=-34.90 |long=-56.15 |label=

2nd goal difference; 3rd goals scored; 4th head-to-head results; 5th draw. |update=complete|source= }} ==Championship playoff== [[Defensor Sporting]] and [[Club Nacional de Football|Nacional]] qualified to the championship playoffs as the Apertura and Clausura winners, respectively. Additionally, Nacional re-qualified as the team with the most points in the season aggregate table. Given this situation, an initial playoff was held between the two teams. Nacional needed to win the playoff to become the season champion; Defensor Sporting needed to win the playoff to force a two-legged final.
